title: Cut a String Into Palindromes
statement:
You get a string s. Cut it into one or more consecutive, non-empty pieces so that every piece is a palindrome: it reads the same left to right and right to left.

Return every way to do this. Each way is the list of its pieces in the order they appear in s, so joining them gives back s. The ways themselves may come in any order.

examples.why: Single letters always work. "oo" and the whole word are palindromes too, but "no" and "noo" are not.
"aba" and "bab" overlap, so no cut can use both. Picking the longest palindrome at each step finds only one of them.
One letter: the only cut is no cut.

hints: Decide the first piece. It must be a palindrome that starts at index 0. What is left to solve afterwards?
After choosing a first piece s[0..i], the rest s[i+1..] is the same problem, only shorter. Try every i where the first piece is a palindrome.
Recurse with a start index. For each end from start to n − 1: if s[start..end] is a palindrome, push it, recurse with end + 1, pop. When start reaches n, record a copy of the pieces.

explain.intuition:
The same template, where a choice is where the next piece ends. A node is a list of pieces covering s[0 .. start − 1]. Its children are all pieces s[start .. end] that are palindromes, for every end from start on. A node is an answer when start reaches the end of the string. Since pieces are always added left to right, every answer comes out in string order and no cut is built twice.

The palindrome test is the pruning: a branch is only entered if its piece is valid, so dead branches are cut at once. Checking a piece with two pointers costs O(n) each time. To save that, precompute a table pal[i][j]: s[i..j] is a palindrome when its end letters match and s[i+1..j−1] is one too. With that, each check is O(1).
steps: Optional: fill pal[i][j] for all i ≤ j, with i going from the end backwards: s[i] === s[j] && (j - i < 2 || pal[i+1][j-1]).
go(start): if start === n, record a copy of pieces and return.
For end from start to n - 1: if s[start..end] is a palindrome, push it, call go(end + 1), pop.
pitfalls: Taking only the longest palindrome at each step. On "abab" that finds ["aba", "b"] and misses the other two.
Recording when a branch has no valid next piece. Only a branch that reached the end of the string is a full cut.
Filling the pal table with i going forwards. pal[i+1][j-1] is then not ready when it is read.

complexity.time: O(n · 2ⁿ): up to 2ⁿ⁻¹ cuts, each copied in O(n)
complexity.space: O(n²) for the table, O(n) for the recursion

solutions.title: Backtracking, checking each piece with two pointers
solutions.idea: Choose where the next piece ends. Enter the branch only if that piece reads the same both ways.

solutions.title: Backtracking with a palindrome table
solutions.idea: Precompute pal[i][j] from shorter ranges to longer ones, so each check during the search is O(1).
